adjudicated.jp: 微笑む少女の胸元に、自然な挙措で手が伸びた。
adjudicated.en: With manners nonchalant my hand extended towards the chest of this smiling girl.
comments: The hand did, not him. This is automatic behavior, see below. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The hand naturally reaches toward the smiling girl's chest. The inverted modifier 'manners nonchalant' is ungrammatical literary affectation, and making the hand the sentence's agent does not require that inversion.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'My hand naturally reached toward the smiling girl's chest.'

highlights.text: With manners nonchalant my hand extended towards the chest of this smiling girl.

adjudicated.jp: 隙を突かれたのか、美希は笑顔のまま身動き一つしなかった。
adjudicated.en: Perhaps because it caught her unaware, Miki didn't make one movement as she stood there smiling.
adjudicated.assessment: Her being caught off guard and remaining completely still while smiling are accurately preserved.
The nonlexical vocalization is represented by an equally nonlexical English sound.

adjudicated.jp: 気がつくと、俺はおっぱいを揉んでいた。
adjudicated.en: When I come to notice, I was rubbing breasts.
comments: He's now de-automatized. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source says that when he realized what he was doing, he was fondling her breasts. 'Come to notice' is unidiomatic, its tense clashes with 'was,' and the English drops the contextual possessor.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'When I came to, I was fondling her breasts.'

highlights.text: When I come to notice, I was rubbing breasts.

adjudicated.jp: ほとんどないと思っていたその「板」には……薄いとはいえ確かな感触が。
adjudicated.en: I flatly thought that there would be about nothing on this Chopping Board... but, weak as it may be, there is certainly that tactile sensation.
comments: OmotteITA sono ITA where ita = board... well at least that was easy to adapt. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source calls her a 'board' he had thought almost entirely flat, then registers a faint but definite softness. 'I flatly thought,' 'about nothing,' and 'weak tactile sensation' are malformed, while capitalizing and specifying 'Chopping Board' distorts the plain insult used for the wordplay.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'That "board" I'd thought was almost perfectly flat... had a faint but unmistakable softness to it.'

highlights.text: I flatly thought that there would be about nothing on this Chopping Board... but, weak as it may be, there is certainly that tactile sensation.

adjudicated.assessment: Her muttered realization of a mistake is functionally conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 笑顔のまま、口元を引きつらせる。
adjudicated.en: Still smiling, the edge of her lips begin to twitch.
adjudicated.assessment: The mouth remains smiling but starts to twitch. The English has a subject-verb disagreement and replaces the natural mouth or corners-of-the-mouth expression with the singular 'edge of her lips.'
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Still smiling, the corners of her mouth began to twitch.'

highlights.text: the edge of her lips begin to twitch

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Sorry, alien hand syndrome, it just went on its own."
comments: The moment when you realize that yes, that's correct, it did... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: He apologizes that his hand moved unconsciously. Naming a neurological syndrome is an unsupported diagnostic joke added by the translation, and the appended clause overexplains the unfinished source line.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Sorry—my hand moved on its own...'

highlights.text: alien hand syndrome, it just went on its own

adjudicated.jp: 「いえ、うっかりしていたわたしが悪いのです」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "No, it's my bad for having been careless."
comments: At least she understands responsibility (in a sense). -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: She accepts blame for having let her guard down; the casual wording preserves the proposition despite modest register drift.

adjudicated.jp: 「あの、こんなこと俺が言うのもなんだけど……ちょっと膨らんでるね。良かったね！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Uhm, I shouldn't exactly be saying this but... they've bulged out a bit. That's great!"
adjudicated.assessment: He awkwardly congratulates her on having filled out a little. 'Bulged out' suggests an abrupt protrusion or swelling rather than modest physical development, making the line harsher and less idiomatic than the source.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'you've filled out a little.'

highlights.text: they've bulged out a bit

adjudicated.jp: 「恐縮です。いつ手を離していただけますでしょうか」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "Much obliged. When will this hand finally distance itself?"
comments: Formal here. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Her mock-politeness asks when he will kindly remove his hand. The English makes the hand an autonomous subject, uses the unidiomatic reflexive 'distance itself,' and loses the pointedly courteous request directed at him.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Much obliged. And when might you remove your hand?'

highlights.text: When will this hand finally distance itself

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "We've finally got some hope for the future here."
comments: Their conversation never crosses here. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: His teasing claim that the future now holds hope is accurately preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「うーん、喜べばいいのか怒ればいいのか。で、いつまで触っておられるつもりでしょうか？」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "Hmmm, should I be happy, should I be angry? Well, for how long do you intend to continue touching this?"
comments: She's not kidding. She literally does not know! -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Her uncertainty between happiness and anger and her formal demand that he stop touching her are both retained.

adjudicated.jp: 「俺は感慨深いよ。あの小さかった、いやさ、平べったかった美希が三次元的立体感を手に入れるなんて」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "I'm deeply moved here. For the so tiny, nay, so tabular Miki has obtained the solid feeling of tridimensionality!"
adjudicated.assessment: The mock-grand statement says that formerly tiny—or rather flat—Miki has acquired three-dimensional volume. The English is syntactically broken after 'For,' and 'tabular' and 'solid feeling of tridimensionality' are technical malapropisms rather than controlled grandiosity.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'To think little—no, flat—Miki has finally acquired three-dimensional volume!'

highlights.text: For the so tiny, nay, so tabular Miki has obtained the solid feeling of tridimensionality

adjudicated.assessment: The silent pause is preserved.
The brief call of her name is exact.

adjudicated.jp: もみもみする手を止めて、顔を見る。
adjudicated.en: I stop the hand going all rubby rubby and look at her face.
adjudicated.assessment: The playful reduplication in the source licenses an informal equivalent for the kneading motion, and the action sequence is preserved.

comments: Maybe she was actually offended at his calling her flat. Certainly, her reaction is not the right one. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The plain statement that she was crying is exact.
His stammered confusion is functionally conveyed.
In the immediate crying context, rendering the choked nonlexical sound as a sniff is a defensible functional cue.
The fragment accurately characterizes the tears as silent and continues syntactically into the next unit.

adjudicated.jp: 嗚咽もなく、頬の曲線を滑りおちる。
adjudicated.en: with sobbing neither, simply slipping down the curve of her cheeks.
adjudicated.assessment: The tears slide down the curve of her cheeks without a sob. 'With sobbing neither' is not grammatical English and obscures the clean continuation from the preceding fragment.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'without a sob, simply slipping down the curve of her cheeks.'

highlights.text: with sobbing neither

adjudicated.jp: 芸術家が美しさに胸打たれて流す涙があるとすれば、これだろう。
adjudicated.en: If I were to imagine the tears flowing from an artist whose heart has been struck by beauty, this would be it.
comments: But is she impressed, or are these just fake? Impossible to understand at this point. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The comparison to an artist moved to tears by beauty is accurately and naturally conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: セクハラされて流すものではない、はず。
adjudicated.en: This is not the shedding of someone subjected to sexual harassment, it can't be.
adjudicated.assessment: His self-serving insistence that these cannot be tears caused by sexual harassment is preserved, despite slightly stiff phrasing.
His confusion is accurately rendered, with the comma carrying the sentence into the following units.
The abrupt stop is accurately rendered as the next clause in the continuing sentence.

comments: It's mostly from Taichi, but it's from both sides in the end. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source gives his inability to understand as the reason he stops. The impersonal 'there's no understanding' replaces that experiencer with an abstract absence and is unnatural in context.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'because I don't understand.'

highlights.text: because there's no understanding

adjudicated.assessment: The hesitant attempt to speak is functionally conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: やがて美希はぐっと涙をぬぐった。
adjudicated.en: Before long Miki well and wiped off her tears,
adjudicated.assessment: Miki soon wipes her tears away firmly. The stray 'well and' makes the sentence ungrammatical and does not convey the decisive force of the adverb.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Before long, Miki firmly wiped away her tears.'

highlights.text: Before long Miki well and wiped off her tears

adjudicated.jp: まぶたの上を腕が往復して、出てきたのはいつもの笑顔。
adjudicated.en: her forearms making a trip around and over her eyelids, and what came out behind them was her smile of always.
comments: 往復, see CCA0015C -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Her arm passes back and forth over her eyelids, revealing her usual smile. The English changes one arm into plural forearms, invents a trip 'around' the eyelids, and ends with the calque 'smile of always.'
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Her arm passed back and forth over her eyes, and out came her usual smile.'

highlights.text: her forearms making a trip around and over her eyelids, and what came out behind them was her smile of always

adjudicated.assessment: The distinctive nonlexical laugh is preserved by transliteration.
She cheerfully turns back to cleaning. 'To cleaning' is not an English idiom for resuming a task and makes the energetic repetition sound malformed.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'All right—back to cleaning, cleaning!'

highlights.text: to cleaning, to cleaning

adjudicated.assessment: Her drawn-out setup and exertion cry are functionally represented.
The forceful pain cry is represented by an equivalent nonlexical shout.

adjudicated.jp: 腕の秘孔（二の腕の中ほどあたり）を一本拳で突かれた。
adjudicated.en: My arm's pressure point (around the center of the forearm) was struck with the exact knuckletip of a fist.
comments: Hokuto no Miki. GIS 一本拳 for what exactly it means. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The parenthetical locates the point around the middle of the upper arm, not the forearm. That anatomical change makes the explicit gloss factually wrong.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'around the middle of my upper arm.'

highlights.text: forearm

adjudicated.jp: 「いたた、筋がすごくいたいよー！　握り拳をぎゅっと作るとピキーンって痛むよー！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "OwChCh, muscle reeeally hurts! When I clench my fist tight it hurts like an electric shooock!"
adjudicated.assessment: The exaggerated complaint that the muscle hurts and that clenching his fist produces a sharp electric pang is functionally preserved.
The source is a compact fragment describing him writhing in agony. The translation adds an inverted finite construction that is neither ordinary narration nor controlled comic diction.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I writhed in agony,' or retain the fragment as 'Me, writhing in agony.'

highlights.text: Writhing in agony go I

comments: Kohaku. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Adapting the lilting cleaning sound into a sung repetition of 'sweep' is a defensible contextual equivalent.
The fragment simply shows Miki cleaning. The subject-verb inversion is unidiomatic and adds an affected cadence absent from the plain source.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Miki went on sweeping.'

highlights.text: sweeping goes Miki

adjudicated.assessment: The abrupt connective is preserved as a deliberately suspended transition.
His incredulous confirmation that she is really Miki is naturally conveyed.
Her brief surprise is preserved.
He says 'No, sorry.' The English replaces the apology with a dismissal that nothing is wrong, changing both the speech act and his stance.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'No—sorry.'

highlights.text: Nah, nothing

adjudicated.jp: 「それは胸があったから美希ではないという意味のご発言でございましょうか？」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "Would that utterance be to the meaning that if I have presence of breasts then I cannot be Miki?"
comments: This continues to sound silly, but see the end of her route: if she changes - grows old - then she stops being what she is.
adjudicated.assessment: Her deliberately formal question asks whether he means she cannot be Miki because she has breasts. 'Be to the meaning' and 'have presence of breasts' are ungrammatical pseudo-formality rather than natural ceremonious English.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Am I to understand that, because I have breasts, I cannot possibly be Miki?'

highlights.text: Would that utterance be to the meaning that if I have presence of breasts then I cannot be Miki

adjudicated.jp: ぺっ、と架空のツバを吐く。
comments: Meaning he didn't actually do it. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The present-tense narration has him mime spitting with an imaginary gob. The adverb 'Imaginarily' is malformed in this use, its capitalization is erroneous, and the translation switches tense.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Pah. I mimed spitting.'

highlights.text: I Imaginarily spat out

adjudicated.assessment: His mock-serious statement of disappointment is accurate.
The comic vocalization of shock is functionally preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「何人の固定ファンを手放したか」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "How many fixated fans did you just lose?"
comments: The reason she isn't too loli (until that new CG in Kiri Sendback that is so loli I could only name the file itself as 'loli') is because Lolicon is a Disease. The word itself isn't exactly strange, but using something that means "fixed" in this story is always suggestive, especially considering this is a metareference. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 固定ファン means established, loyal, or dedicated fans. 'Fixated fans' instead describes people obsessively attached and changes a marketing-style category into a psychological judgment.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'How many dedicated fans do you think you just lost?'

highlights.text: fixated fans

adjudicated.assessment: The repeated term refers to loyal or dedicated fans, not fans who are fixated. The error is repeated here as dialogue terminology.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Dedicated fans?'

highlights.text: Fixated fans

adjudicated.jp: 「たとえロリっ娘でなくとも胸がないことで、幼稚園児をその聖域とする社会不適合者の支持を受けることも不可能ではないのに……」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Because it's not impossible you've been receiving the endorsement of those societally nonconforming people who make the kindergarten into their Holy Ground due to your having a flat chest, even if you aren't exactly loli..."
comments: And here's more from where that Fixated came from: "noncomforming" is the PC word for "people in Gunjou". I THINK TANAKA IS SAYING SOMETHING HERE TO PEOPLE WITH LOLICON BUT I WOULDN'T KNOW WHAT. And he's still being comparatively nice than to the Big Purty Words Mean Good Writing crowd. Also, notice the unsubtle way in which Taichi puts himself in this. See CCA0013: he was trying to groom Miki as he did Yusa. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source describes social misfits who treat kindergarten-aged children as their sacred domain. The English changes the children, 幼稚園児, into the institution 'the kindergarten,' materially altering the target of the grotesque joke.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'who regard kindergarteners as their sacred domain.'

highlights.text: make the kindergarten into their Holy Ground

adjudicated.en: Miki: "It's just the end of the world here!"
comments: Another of those cough-cough lines. Curiously, it appears Buddhist... but then again, Miki's known to pilfer from dem Christians, isn't she. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The idiomatic lament that the world has come to this is conveyed by an equivalent end-of-the-world complaint.

adjudicated.jp: 「美希のばかっ、セクハラしちゃってごめんよ！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Miki you dummy, sorry for sexually harassing you!"
comments: Regression to tsundere. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The simultaneous insult and apology for the harassment are directly preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 罵声と謝罪を同時にこなして、俺は走り去る。
adjudicated.en: Managing simultaneous words of scorn and of apology, I run away.
comments: This may be his reaction to her using a Buddhist aphorism. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The narration accurately states that he combines abuse and apology before running away.

comments: CP 'bove He thought it twice again. -GHS
